title: Rolling prewarm and evacuation scheduler for tiered throughput guarantees
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: Dedicated capacity customers expect both strict throughput guarantees and low-risk maintenance windows. Current rolling-drain flows are causing measurable tail-latency spikes when large KV caches must be warmed after node reclamation. This ticket implements a scheduler that coordinates staged prewarm lanes, soft-eviction tokens, and eviction pacing tied to SLO-aware throughput contracts so we can perform upgrades and maintenance without violating per-tenant throughput guarantees.

Scope: Design and implement a fleet-level scheduler that: (1) earmarks a small fraction of capacity as 'prewarm lanes' prior to planned drains; (2) issues short-lived soft-eviction tokens to hosts to begin background KV preheat and model shard warmup in compatible hosts; (3) coordinates eviction pacing so that throughput reservations are honored while rolling upgrades proceed; (4) exposes controls in the autoscaler and the Console for configuring prewarm fraction, max simultaneous evictions, and warmup timeout; (5) emits metrics and traces for per-tenant throughput adherence and warmup progress.

Goals:
- Avoid >5% SLO breach during scheduled maintenance for tenants with pinned throughput reservations.
- Reduce median KV-warmup time by enabling background preheating on target hosts prior to traffic handover.
- Provide operators explicit knobs to trade maintenance speed versus customer throughput stability.

Design notes:
- Prewarm lanes: pick N hosts (configurable percentage) in the target shard and mark them as candidates for preheating. Use low-impact background CPU/GPU limits for warmup so host capacity is still available for low-priority work.
- Soft-eviction tokens: when a node is scheduled for drain, the scheduler issues tokens to target hosts that allow them to fetch KV segments, populate local caches, and materialize compressed model weights (if needed). Tokens expire after a configurable timeout to avoid unbounded prefill.
- Eviction pacing: implement a per-shard token bucket representing throughput reservations. Evictions consume tokens; when the bucket doesn't have capacity, eviction is deferred. This ensures tenants with throughput commitments keep reserved capacity until a safe handover window.
- Autoscaler integration: the scheduler will signal to the autoscaler to temporarily hold or grow spare capacity in a target region when prewarm fraction is above 0.
- Observability: add metrics for prewarm_progress, token_issuance_rate, eviction_wait_seconds, and per-tenant throughput_delta_during_maintenance. Provide a Console view showing ongoing maintenance waves and estimated time-to-safe-handover.

Non-goals: offline data migration, model loading optimizations beyond prefill orchestration, or tenants without throughput reservations (these will use best-effort fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can allocate prewarm lanes and issue soft-eviction tokens on a test fleet
Eviction pacing prevents throughput reservation breaches during a simulated rolling upgrade (SLO breach < 5%)
Telemetry surfaces token lifecycle and warmup progress in Console dashboards
Autoscaler respects scheduler signals and can spin up temporary spare capacity when requested
Operational runbook documented and tested with a canary upgrade on staging
